meta.title: Charlotte-Area Young Adult Resource Navigator
meta.description: A researched working directory of reputable resources in Charlotte, surrounding communities within roughly 30 miles, and essential statewide or national fallback programs.
meta.radiusDefinition: Local results are grouped by service location within roughly 30 road miles of Uptown Charlotte. This is a practical service-area screen, not a precise geospatial guarantee.

triage.situation: Immediate danger, overdose, violence or serious injury
triage.backup: Use Safe Alliance, trafficking or crisis resources after immediate safety is addressed.
triage.limit: Do not use a routine referral process for an active emergency.

triage.situation: Suicidal thoughts or acute mental health crisis
triage.limit: Call 911 when there is immediate danger or a medical emergency.

triage.situation: Homeless tonight or unsafe place to sleep
triage.backup: Ages 16–24: The Relatives On Ramp; men: Roof Above; women/children: Center of Hope.
triage.limit: Beds and housing are limited; assessment does not guarantee placement.

triage.backup: Ask about VPA, GEAR Up, Medicaid and foster-specific education funds.
triage.limit: Many benefits end at 21; act quickly.

triage.backup: Use NC 211 and Mecklenburg Community Resource Centers for additional benefits.
triage.limit: Call before traveling; hours and capacity change.

triage.backup: Call 911 for immediate danger; Legal Aid/Charlotte Legal Advocacy for civil legal help.
triage.limit: Protect confidential location and contact information.

triage.situation: No food or basic household items
triage.firstAction: Apply for SNAP and contact Nourish Up
triage.backup: Crisis Assistance Free Store; Second Harvest food locator.
triage.limit: Emergency food should be paired with a longer-term benefits plan.

triage.situation: A young adult needs counseling or emotional support related to identity, relationships or sexuality
triage.firstAction: Mental Health America of Central Carolinas — Counseling
triage.backup: The Barnabas Center also provides professional counseling with a faith-based option. The 988 Lifeline provides immediate crisis support, and 911 is appropriate for immediate danger.
triage.limit: Counseling availability and fit vary. The young adult or support person should call first to ask about openings, cost and whether the counselor can meet the identified needs.

fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Young people who are or were in foster care in Mecklenburg County; county rules apply.
fosterPrograms.primaryValue: Help planning for housing, school, work and living on their own, plus some financial assistance.
fosterPrograms.recommendedAction: Contact LINKS as early as possible and document the young adult's foster-care history.

fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Former Mecklenburg County foster youth who are no longer in county care; individual eligibility must be confirmed.
fosterPrograms.primaryValue: Transition support after foster care, including access to eligible financial assistance.
fosterPrograms.recommendedAction: Call 704-336-3290 before the young adult's 21st birthday.

fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Young adults who meet North Carolina requirements and sign a voluntary placement agreement.
fosterPrograms.primaryValue: Continued placement, planning support and financial assistance through age 21.
fosterPrograms.recommendedAction: Contact LINKS before discharge from foster care and complete the agreement before leaving care.

fosterPrograms.program: Medicaid for Former Foster Care Youth
fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Certain young adults who were in foster care and had Medicaid when they aged out; state rules apply.
fosterPrograms.primaryValue: Health coverage for medical care, prescriptions and mental health care.
fosterPrograms.recommendedAction: State former foster-care status clearly on the application.

fosterPrograms.ageWindow: Often under 26 for eligible former foster youth
fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Medicaid members who meet the plan's child-welfare or former-foster-care requirements.
fosterPrograms.primaryValue: A Medicaid plan designed for people with foster-care experience, including help coordinating health care.
fosterPrograms.recommendedAction: Confirm plan enrollment and keep contact information current.

fosterPrograms.ageWindow: College or career training; current program rules apply
fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Eligible North Carolina residents who aged out at 18 or were adopted after age 12 and attend an eligible public school at least half time.
fosterPrograms.primaryValue: Scholarship support for approved school costs remaining after other financial aid.
fosterPrograms.recommendedAction: Complete the FAFSA and NC Reach application before classes begin.

fosterPrograms.ageWindow: Age and foster-care status rules apply
fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Eligible current or former foster youth and some young people who left care through adoption or guardianship.
fosterPrograms.primaryValue: Funding for approved college, career-school and training costs, up to the program limit.
fosterPrograms.recommendedAction: Coordinate ETV with LINKS and the school's financial-aid office.

fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Young adults preparing to leave or recently leaving foster care who meet local referral criteria.
fosterPrograms.primaryValue: One-on-one support with housing, employment, education, money and daily life.
fosterPrograms.recommendedAction: Contact the Charlotte-area program and confirm the referral pathway and current openings.

fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Mecklenburg County young people ages 16–24; foster-care history is not required.
fosterPrograms.primaryValue: One place for planning and connections to housing, work, school and basic-needs support.
fosterPrograms.recommendedAction: Use On Ramp when a young adult has several needs or needs help deciding where to start.

fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Young adults ages 18–24 who are homeless, at risk of losing housing or fleeing violence; screening applies.
fosterPrograms.primaryValue: Housing in community apartments plus support with goals and everyday needs.
fosterPrograms.recommendedAction: Request screening early; placement depends on available openings.

fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Young people in foster care who meet the program's matching criteria.
fosterPrograms.primaryValue: Long-term volunteer mentoring and consistent relational support.
fosterPrograms.recommendedAction: Coordinate with existing mentors to avoid overlapping or conflicting roles.

fosterPrograms.ageWindow: Teens through the mid-20s, depending on the activity
fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Young people with foster care, kinship care, group-home or other out-of-home-care experience.
fosterPrograms.primaryValue: Peer community, leadership opportunities, advocacy and transition information.
fosterPrograms.recommendedAction: Confirm eligibility for the activity and invite young adults who want peer connection and leadership opportunities.

fosterPrograms.ageWindow: Young people without safe, stable housing
fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Young people experiencing homelessness who need help getting an ID, birth certificate or another important document.
fosterPrograms.primaryValue: Free legal help obtaining IDs and important documents.
fosterPrograms.recommendedAction: Call or text 1-888-870-DOCS and confirm the current hours.

fosterPrograms.ageWindow: Different tracks for teens, young adults and people over 20
fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Young people transitioning from foster care or adolescence; current enrollment and age-track rules apply.
fosterPrograms.primaryValue: Mentoring, coaching, money skills, leadership and practical living skills.
fosterPrograms.recommendedAction: Ask about the current virtual group and the track that fits the young adult's age.

fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Young women aging out of foster care who meet the program's current criteria.
fosterPrograms.primaryValue: Workshops, supportive relationships and connections to education, employment and stability resources.
fosterPrograms.recommendedAction: Confirm current programming and do not describe housing as available unless staff confirms it.

fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Young people under 18 currently in foster care through Mecklenburg or Union County.
fosterPrograms.primaryValue: A committed adult mentor before the transition out of foster care.
fosterPrograms.recommendedAction: Use for planning before age 18 and coordinate clearly with any other mentor.

fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Students with foster-care or emancipation experience who are interested in Livingstone College.
fosterPrograms.primaryValue: A foster-specific college recruitment and support pathway developed with Home4Me.
fosterPrograms.recommendedAction: Contact the project before applying and confirm current financial, housing and student-retention support.
